New columns (projected_end_date, intervention_id) and the metric_definitions table have no migration. Base.metadata.create_all never ALTERs an existing main.db, so upgrading users either hit 'no such column' errors or keep old rows with NULL intervention_id that the new intervention-scoped views no longer show. Add a schema-version migration that ALTERs the tables and backfills or surfaces legacy

The manual date-range summary filters metrics to intervention_id IS NULL. Since the normal logging flow now always sets intervention_id, a manual range reports no metrics even when entries exist in that range, contradicting the README promise to summarize all metrics within a manual date range.

The manual date-range summary filters events to intervention_id IS NULL, so events logged against an intervention are omitted from the range summary. Include all events whose timestamp falls in the selected range.

The UI always reports 'Settings have been saved' after calling settings_manager.save_settings(), but that method swallows IOError and only logs it. A failed write therefore tells the user their settings were persisted when they were not; return success from the manager and show the error on failure.

Renaming a MetricDefinition updates only the definition, not existing MetricEntry.metric_name rows. The same metric then appears under two names, and the logging dropdown and plot selector disagree. Update matching entries in the same transaction or make the definition name immutable.
The Dict annotation at line 20 is used without importing Dict; only Optional is imported. Add Dict to the typing import so static checkers and any future runtime annotation evaluation resolve it.
